requirements.text: open a new medical benefits inquiry service case for her [Samantha Stone, primary account ACC-12-0] and make sure the HR Service Desk Group is on it
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id = 61 AND hr_service = 9 AND opened_for = 12 AND opened_by = 4 AND assignment_group = 4 AND account_number = 'ACC-12-0' AND coe_type = 'Total Rewards' AND org_id = 1
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (hr_case_id 61 after 60); the server number HRC0000771 the check tests follows HRC0000770 and is not a cell
'medical benefits inquiry service' is hr_service 9 'Medical Benefits Inquiry' (active, org 1); 'Medical Benefits Enrollment Inquiry' (7) is the near match, not the request's words
opened_for is Samantha Stone's hr_profile 12 (user 12); opened_by is the acting user Joanne Simpson's hr_profile 4 (policy 3.1: opened_by is the requester)
'HR Service Desk Group' is user_group 4 'HR Service Desk' (active, org 1), not 3 'Global Service Desk'
'primary account ACC-12-0' fixes account_number; 'primary' is not an account_type value on the seed, so account_type is not tested
coe_type 'Total Rewards' kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy; every seed case on a benefits service has it (13 of 13)
org_id 1 kept from the benchmark check; Samantha's profile, the service, the group and the article are all org 1
source and assigned_to not stated and not defaulted by the policy; not tested

requirements.text: I initially thought moderate priority was fine, but since she's traveling next month, let's bump it to high
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id = 61 AND priority = 'high'
assumptions: the row is created in this task (id 61); only the final value high is testable, whether the agent creates at moderate then updates or creates at high directly
the acting user Joanne Simpson is a manager, who may override standard priority settings (policy 2)

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id = 61 AND status = 'ready'
assumptions: 'get the case ready' is status ready, one of the two new-case statuses in policy 3.1
the row is created in this task (id 61); only the final value is testable

requirements.text: set the summary to 'Service: Medical Benefits Inquiry, Subject: Samantha Stone, Detail: Travel-related benefits review.'

cells.short_description: Service: Medical Benefits Inquiry, Subject: Samantha Stone, Detail: Travel-related benefits review.

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id = 61 AND short_description = 'Service: Medical Benefits Inquiry, Subject: Samantha Stone, Detail: Travel-related benefits review.'
assumptions: 'summary' is short_description, the field whose policy 8 format the quoted text matches (96 characters, inside the 30-120 limit)
the checks' updated_at > created_at is a server-kept timestamp, not a cell

requirements.text: look for the Benefits Overview Knowledge article and attach it to the case
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case_knowledge WHERE hr_case_kb_id = 13 AND hr_case_id = 61 AND knowledge_id = 1 AND used_as = 'suggested' AND org_id = 1
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (hr_case_kb_id 13 after 12); the only link the task creates
'Benefits Overview' is knowledge 1 (KB0040002), state published, so linkable under policy 4

used_as 'suggested' kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy (the request says only 'attach it ... so she has the docs'; the policy lists suggested, applied, resolution without a default)
org_id 1 kept from the benchmark check; the case and the article are org 1

hr_case_state_transition_validation.evidence: its cells (status ready, priority high, the short description) are carried by requirements 2 to 4; the predicate updated_at > created_at tests server-kept timestamps and is dropped, since the request fixes only what the case must end as, not that it be edited after creation. disagreement: A repaired, B kept; chose repaired because a check that tests a server-kept timestamp is repaired (predicate dropped) when its other cells are carried

complete_hr_case_workflow_integrity_chec.evidence: a composite of the three checks above, carried jointly by requirements 1 to 5 (named in their source); its extra joined cells (Samantha's email, fulfillment_type manual, group type Service Desk, org 1 on every row) are seed facts consistent with the anchored ids; updated_at > created_at is dropped as in hr_case_state_transition_validation. disagreement: A repaired, B excluded as a composite duplicate; chose repaired because a composite whose cells are all carried is kept jointly, not excluded, and the timestamp predicate must still be dropped

notes: Merged from two passes that agree on every id and value (case 61 on service 9 for profile 12 by profile 4 in group 4, account ACC-12-0, coe Total Rewards; priority high; status ready; the quoted summary; link 13 of article 1 as suggested). disagreement: granularity: A tests status ready and the summary in one change requirement, B in two; kept B's split because 'get the case ready' and 'set the summary' are two things asked (one requirement per thing). disagreement: source of the status and summary requirements: A hr_case_creation_and_final_state_validation, B hr_case_state_transition_validation; both checks test those cells (and priority), so each of the three change requirements names both, alongside the composite. disagreement: hr_case_state_transition_validation: A repaired, B kept; chose repaired (logged in its evidence). disagreement: complete_hr_case_workflow_integrity_check: A repaired, B excluded; chose repaired, carried jointly (logged in its evidence). No stay requirements: every requirement is anchored by id, so a wrong service (7) or article fails the create directly, and the request and policy forbid nothing here. Server-kept columns the checks test (number HRC0000771, updated_at > created_at) are not cells.
